questions.question: In triangle $PQR$, $\angle P = 38^\circ$, side $p = QR = 9$ cm, and side $r = PQ = 7$ cm. Determine whether triangle $PQR$ can be formed. If yes, find $\angle R$.
questions.referenceAnswer:
1. By the sine formula: $\frac{7\ \text{cm}}{\sin R} = \frac{9\ \text{cm}}{\sin 38^\circ}$
2. Solve for $\sin R$: $\sin R = \frac{7 \sin 38^\circ}{9}$
3. Compute: $\sin 38^\circ \approx 0.6157$, so $\sin R = \frac{7 \times 0.6157}{9} \approx 0.4793$
4. Since $0.4793 < 1$, a solution exists.
5. $R = \arcsin(0.4793) \approx 28.6^\circ$
6. Check angle sum: $P + R = 38^\circ + 28.6^\circ = 66.6^\circ < 180^\circ$, and obtuse $R = 151.4^\circ$ gives $P + R = 189.4^\circ > 180^\circ$, so only one valid solution.
Answer: $28.6^\circ$

questions.question: In triangle $XYZ$, $\angle X = 110^\circ$, side $x = YZ = 15$ cm, and side $z = XY = 8$ cm. Determine whether triangle $XYZ$ can be formed. If yes, find $\angle Z$.
questions.referenceAnswer:
1. By the sine formula: $\frac{8\ \text{cm}}{\sin Z} = \frac{15\ \text{cm}}{\sin 110^\circ}$
2. Solve for $\sin Z$: $\sin Z = \frac{8 \sin 110^\circ}{15}$
3. Compute: $\sin 110^\circ = \sin(70^\circ) \approx 0.9397$
4. So $\sin Z = \frac{8 \times 0.9397}{15} \approx 0.5012$
5. Since $0.5012 < 1$, a solution exists.
6. $Z = \arcsin(0.5012) \approx 30.1^\circ$ (obtuse $Z = 149.9^\circ$ gives $X + Z > 180^\circ$, invalid).
Answer: $30.1^\circ$

questions.question: In triangle $LMN$, $\angle L = 22^\circ$, side $l = MN = 6$ cm, and side $n = LM = 5$ cm. Determine whether triangle $LMN$ can be formed. If yes, find $\angle N$.
questions.referenceAnswer:
1. By the sine formula: $\frac{5\ \text{cm}}{\sin N} = \frac{6\ \text{cm}}{\sin 22^\circ}$
2. Solve for $\sin N$: $\sin N = \frac{5 \sin 22^\circ}{6}$
3. Compute: $\sin 22^\circ \approx 0.3746$, so $\sin N = \frac{5 \times 0.3746}{6} \approx 0.3122$
4. Since $0.3122 < 1$, a solution exists.
